newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - House of Fraser set to smarten up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - House of Fraser set to smarten up.

text.p: British department store group House of Fraser Plc, is expected to post flat underlying profits when it reports annual results next Thursday, but it could show that new management and new-look stores are starting to smarten up its performance, retail analysts said.

Pretax profits for the year to January 25, 1997, excluding exceptional costs, are forecast between 14.0 and 15.0 million stg, against 14.3 million a year ago. The dividend is expected to be unchanged at 5.5 pence a share.
The results will include exceptional costs of around 40 to 50 million stg, already flagged in January, when the group announced sweeping cost cuts, including a major clearout of old stock.

In January the group said it would axe around 1,000 jobs and sell three stores as part of the rationalisation. The retailer has performed poorly since the Fayed brothers owners of Harrods floated the company in 1994. It made a first half loss of 13.6 million stg.
Its stores have struggled, while rivals such as John Lewis and Debenhams have been storming ahead.
The retailer, with 51 stores across Britain, is trying to reverse its decline by attacking costs and revamping its buying strategy.
Its shares, at 165 pence on Friday morning, have perked up ahead of the figures, but are still well below the group's 1994 flotation price of 180 pence.

Chief executive John Coleman has overhauled management and introduced low-cost refurbishments to update some of the dowdier shops, including four recently completed at Leamington Spa, Carlisle, Milton Keynes and Thurrock.

Analysts said refurbishment of the Leeds store in northern England last year had produced a strong sales uplift, with some estimating as much as a 40 percent increase. This has raised expectations the four recently refurbished stores can liven up their performance.
"I would expect some positive results from the four others," said Roy Maconochie, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
But results of a radical revamp of womenswear ranges will not be known until later in the year as the clothes do not come into the shops until the autumn.
"The real test comes in the autumn when they will have the majority of the merchandise as they want it," said another retail analyst.
Opinions are divided on the chances of a significant turnaround. Maconochie at Henderson Crosthwaite rates the shares a buy, while others prefer "hold", at best.
Some see the shares as a strong sell. They argue that more stores will have to go, and see the recovery arriving too late in the economic cycle to produce the hoped-for upturn.
"It's a difficult time to try and improve the performance, when interest rates may soon rise," said another retail analyst.
